questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The committee discussed about / the draft policy / for nearly two hours.
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'The committee discussed about'. 'Discuss' is transitive: 'discussed the draft policy'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said to me, "I am working on the report now."
o: He told me that he was working on the report then.
He told me that he is working on the report now.
He told me that I was working on the report then.
He said me that he was working on the report then.
questions.x: Correct answer: He told me that he was working on the report then.. Tense moves back and 'now' becomes 'then'; 'said to' becomes 'told'.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
She did not know (where was the file kept).
questions.x: Correct answer: where the file was kept. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: If a company is said to be 'in the red' this quarter, it is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Making a loss. 'In the red' refers to losses or debt.

questions.q: You ____ submit the nomination form today; the deadline is next month.
questions.x: 'Need not' shows absence of necessity; 'must not' would forbid it.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to 'legitimate' as used in: 'The tribunal found the workers' demands legitimate.'
questions.x: Correct answer: Unjustified. Legitimate: justified or lawful.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
She is one of those officers who (has served) in three different States.
questions.x: Correct answer: have served. 'Who' refers to 'officers' (plural), so the verb is plural.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The cashier denied / to have taken / the missing amount.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'to have taken'. 'Deny' takes a gerund: 'denied having taken'.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: 'The meeting ended in a deafening silence.'
questions.x: Correct answer: Oxymoron. 'Deafening' and 'silence' are contradictory terms placed together.

questions.q:
Rearrange the following sentences (P, Q, R, S) to form a coherent paragraph:
P: But the price soon crashed as many farmers had planted the same crop.
Q: Last year onion prices rose sharply.
R: Individual decisions based on current prices can thus create the next glut.
S: Encouraged by this, farmers expanded the area under onion this season.
questions.x: Correct answer: QSPR. Rise in price → expansion → crash → lesson.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The committee's report was a scathing indictment of the department', the word 'scathing' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Severely critical. Scathing: harshly critical.

questions.q: The revised wage rates will ____ from the first of next month.
questions.x: 'Come into effect' means begin to apply.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The cattle / is grazing / in the open field.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'is grazing'. 'Cattle' is plural: 'are grazing'.

questions.q: The phrase 'becomes a ritual rather than a choice' suggests that frequent consent requests:
o: Make people more careful about privacy
Lead people to agree mechanically without real understanding
Give people more control over data
questions.x: Answer: 'Lead people to agree mechanically without real understanding'. People click without reading. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Every application now asks for consent, and almost everyone clicks 'I agree' without reading. Consent that is demanded dozens of times a day becomes a ritual rather than a choice. Placing the whole burden of privacy on the individual assumes that people have the time and expertise to judge complex data practices. A better approach would also place duties on those who collect data: to gather only what is needed, to keep it no longer than necessary, and to answer for its misuse.

questions.q: The author proposes that data collectors should:
o: Collect only necessary data, retain it briefly and be accountable for misuse
Sell data only to government agencies
questions.x: Answer: 'Collect only necessary data, retain it briefly and be accountable for misuse'. These duties are listed in the last sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Every application now asks for consent, and almost everyone clicks 'I agree' without reading. Consent that is demanded dozens of times a day becomes a ritual rather than a choice. Placing the whole burden of privacy on the individual assumes that people have the time and expertise to judge complex data practices. A better approach would also place duties on those who collect data: to gather only what is needed, to keep it no longer than necessary, and to answer for its misuse.

questions.q: Which assumption does the author criticise?
o: That individuals can judge complex data practices on their own
questions.x: Answer: 'That individuals can judge complex data practices on their own'. The author questions placing 'the whole burden' on individuals. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Every application now asks for consent, and almost everyone clicks 'I agree' without reading. Consent that is demanded dozens of times a day becomes a ritual rather than a choice. Placing the whole burden of privacy on the individual assumes that people have the time and expertise to judge complex data practices. A better approach would also place duties on those who collect data: to gather only what is needed, to keep it no longer than necessary, and to answer for its misuse.

questions.q: The expression 'reads sources against the grain' means:
o: Accepting every statement at face value
Questioning sources for their biases and omissions
questions.x: Answer: 'Questioning sources for their biases and omissions'. It means looking beyond the surface, including what is left out. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Historians cannot simply read the past off documents. Every source was produced by someone with a purpose: a court chronicler praising a king, an official defending a policy, a traveller seeking to impress readers at home. Silence, too, is evidence; the lives of peasants and women often survive only in the margins. Good history therefore reads sources against the grain, asking not only what they say but also what they leave out and why.

questions.q: According to the passage, why is 'silence' also evidence?
o: What is left out reveals whose lives and views were ignored
Documents were written in silent rooms
questions.x: Answer: 'What is left out reveals whose lives and views were ignored'. Peasants and women survive 'only in the margins'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Historians cannot simply read the past off documents. Every source was produced by someone with a purpose: a court chronicler praising a king, an official defending a policy, a traveller seeking to impress readers at home. Silence, too, is evidence; the lives of peasants and women often survive only in the margins. Good history therefore reads sources against the grain, asking not only what they say but also what they leave out and why.

questions.q: The examples of the court chronicler and the traveller illustrate that:
o: Sources reflect the purposes of those who produced them
questions.x: Answer: 'Sources reflect the purposes of those who produced them'. Each produced writing 'with a purpose'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Historians cannot simply read the past off documents. Every source was produced by someone with a purpose: a court chronicler praising a king, an official defending a policy, a traveller seeking to impress readers at home. Silence, too, is evidence; the lives of peasants and women often survive only in the margins. Good history therefore reads sources against the grain, asking not only what they say but also what they leave out and why.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Dadabhai Naoroji:
1. He wrote 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.
2. He was elected to the British House of Commons.
3. He presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session (1885).

questions.q:
Match the classical dance with its State of origin:
Dance:
A. Sattriya
B. Mohiniyattam
C. Kuchipudi
D. Odissi
State:
1. Odisha
2. Kerala
3. Andhra Pradesh
4. Assam
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Sattriya) → 4 (Assam); B (Mohiniyattam) → 2 (Kerala); C (Kuchipudi) → 3 (Andhra Pradesh); D (Odissi) → 1 (Odisha).
Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises eight classical dances.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman president of the Congress.
2. Annie Besant founded the Home Rule League in Madras.
3. Kasturba Gandhi presided over the Lahore session of 1929.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Lahore session.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Harappan civilisation:
1. Its cities show planned streets and drainage.
2. Dholavira is known for its water management system.
3. Its script has been fully deciphered.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Indus script remains undeciphered.

questions.q: Arrange the following uprisings in chronological order: 1. Santhal Hul 2. Rampa rebellion led by Alluri Sitarama Raju 3. Deccan Riots 4. Paika rebellion
questions.x: Paika (1817), Santhal Hul (1855–56), Deccan Riots (1875), Rampa (1922–24).

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Cripps Mission 2. Wavell Plan 3. Mountbatten Plan 4. Cabinet Mission

Consider the following about the Self-Respect Movement:
1. It was founded by E. V. Ramasamy (Periyar).
2. It promoted marriages without Brahmin priests.
3. It supported the caste hierarchy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It opposed caste hierarchy.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Doctrine of Lapse:
1. It was applied by Lord Dalhousie.
2. Satara was the first state annexed under it.
3. Awadh was annexed under it in 1856.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Awadh was annexed on the ground of alleged misgovernment, not lapse.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of monument and ruler is correctly matched?
questions.x: Qutb Minar was begun by Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish; the Red Fort and Taj Mahal were built by Shah Jahan.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Surat split 2. Partition of Bengal 3. Morley–Minto reforms 4. Annulment of Partition of Bengal

Consider the following about the Karachi session (1931):
1. It endorsed the Gandhi–Irwin Pact.
2. It adopted resolutions on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme.
3. It was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Vallabhbhai Patel presided.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the INA trials (1945–46):
1. They were held at the Red Fort.
2. Bhulabhai Desai was among the defence counsel.
3. The trials aroused widespread public sympathy across communities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct; the accused included Shah Nawaz Khan, P. K. Sahgal and G. S. Dhillon.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): MoSPI began releasing monthly unemployment estimates from the PLFS in 2025.
Reason (R): Monthly estimates are based on the Current Weekly Status approach.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; R explains the method, not why monthly releases began.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Mission Mausam:
1. It aims to make India 'weather-ready and climate-smart'.
2. It is implemented through IMD, IITM and NCMRWF.
3. It is run by the Ministry of Agriculture.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Aspirational Blocks Programme:
1. It was launched in 2023 to improve governance in about 500 blocks.
2. It is modelled on the Aspirational Districts Programme.
3. It replaces the Aspirational Districts Programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The district programme continues.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Rail-based launchers improve the survivability of strategic missiles.
Reason (R): Missiles on rail networks can move across the country and launch with short reaction time.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Mobility makes them hard to target.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's trade agreements in 2025:
1. India and the UK signed a Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement in July 2025.
2. The India–EFTA TEPA entered into force on 1 October 2025.
3. India rejoined negotiations for RCEP in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India has not rejoined RCEP.

questions.q:
Consider the following about global environmental negotiations in 2025:
1. Talks in Geneva on a global plastics treaty ended without agreement.
2. The International Court of Justice gave an advisory opinion on States' obligations on climate change.
3. The Paris Agreement was formally replaced by a new treaty at COP30.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Paris Agreement remains in force.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's ranking in 2025 reports:
1. India entered the top 100 of the UN Sustainable Development Report for the first time.
2. India remained in the bottom half of the Global Gender Gap Index.
3. India topped the Human Development Index among South Asian countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Sri Lanka and the Maldives rank above India in the HDI.

questions.q:
Consider the following about GST reforms in 2025:
1. From 22 September 2025, a two-slab structure of 5% and 18% replaced most of the earlier slabs.
2. A special rate of 40% applies to specified sin and luxury goods.
3. Petrol and diesel were brought under GST.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Petroleum products remain outside GST.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Maha Kumbh 2025:
1. It was held at Prayagraj.
2. It is held at the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati.
3. It is held every six years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A Maha Kumbh at Prayagraj comes after twelve Kumbh cycles; Ardh Kumbh is held every six years.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's space missions in 2025:
1. SpaDeX demonstrated docking of two satellites in January 2025.
2. NISAR, a joint ISRO–NASA mission, was launched in July 2025.
3. Shubhanshu Shukla became the first Indian to travel to the International Space Station.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three occurred in 2025.

questions.q: NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index (2025) evaluates:
o: States on parameters such as quality of expenditure, revenue mobilisation, fiscal prudence and debt sustainability
questions.x: Correct answer: States on parameters such as quality of expenditure, revenue mobilisation, fiscal prudence and debt sustainability. Larger States were ranked on fiscal health indicators.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. On dissolution of the House, the Speaker remains in office until the new House first meets.
2. The President appoints the pro tem Speaker.
3. The Speaker resigns by writing to the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Speaker addresses the resignation to the Deputy Speaker.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the election of the Vice-President:
1. The electoral college consists of all members (elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament.
2. Members of State Legislative Assemblies also vote.
3. The election is by proportional representation by single transferable vote and secret ballot.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
State legislators vote in the presidential election, not in the vice-presidential election.

questions.q: Which feature was borrowed from the Irish Constitution?
o: Directive Principles of State Policy and method of election of the President
questions.x: The Irish Constitution also inspired nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q:
Match the writ with the situation in which it is ordinarily used:
Writ:
A. Mandamus
B. Prohibition
C. Certiorari
D. Quo warranto
Use:
1. Inquiring into the legality of a claim to a public office
2. Stopping a lower court from exceeding jurisdiction in a pending case
3. Quashing an order already passed by a lower court or tribunal
4. Compelling an official to perform a statutory duty
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Mandamus) → 4 (Compelling an official to perform a statutory duty); B (Prohibition) → 2 (Stopping a lower court from exceeding jurisdiction in a pending case); C (Certiorari) → 3 (Quashing an order already passed by a lower court or tribunal); D (Quo warranto) → 1 (Inquiring into the legality of a claim to a public office).
Prohibition is preventive; certiorari is both preventive and curative.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Parliamentary privileges:
1. No member is liable to court proceedings for anything said in Parliament.
2. Members are free from arrest in civil cases during the session and 40 days before and after.
3. Members are immune from arrest in criminal cases during the session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Privilege from arrest does not extend to criminal cases.

questions.q:
With reference to Money Bills, consider the following:
1. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President.
2. The Rajya Sabha can reject a Money Bill.
3. The Speaker's certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill is endorsed on it when sent to the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
The Rajya Sabha can only recommend amendments within 14 days.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Comptroller and Auditor General:
1. The CAG's salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The CAG is not eligible for further office under the Government after ceasing to hold office.
3. The CAG submits reports on State accounts to the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Articles 148 and 151.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Uniform Civil Code:
1. Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure a UCC throughout the territory of India.
2. Uttarakhand implemented a UCC law in 2025.
3. Goa has had a common civil code since before its integration with India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about appointment of Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act:
1. The selection committee consists of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition (or leader of the largest opposition party) and a Union Cabinet Minister.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge.
3. The Chief Justice of India is a member of the selection committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The 2023 Act replaced the interim arrangement (which had included the CJI) set by the Supreme Court in Anoop Baranwal.

questions.q: The 16th Finance Commission, chaired by Arvind Panagariya, covers the award period:
questions.x: Correct answer: 2026–27 to 2030–31. The 15th FC covered 2021–26.

questions.q: Which judgment restored the collegium system by striking down the National Judicial Appointments Commission?
o: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015)
questions.x: Correct answer: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015). The Fourth Judges Case struck down the 99th Amendment.

questions.q: Arrange the following constitutional amendments in chronological order: 1. Anti-defection law 2. Reduction of voting age to 18 3. Panchayati Raj 4. GST

With reference to the PESA Act, 1996, consider the following:
1. It extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas with modifications.
2. It gives Gram Sabhas powers over minor forest produce.
3. It applies to Sixth Schedule areas of the North-East.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Sixth Schedule areas have Autonomous District Councils.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Union Budget 2025–26:
1. It targeted a fiscal deficit of 4.4% of GDP.
2. Under the new tax regime, income up to ₹12 lakh (excluding special-rate income) effectively bears no tax.
3. It raised the MSME investment and turnover limits for classification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are features of the 2025–26 Budget.

questions.q:
Consider the following about multidimensional poverty measurement:
1. NITI Aayog's index uses health, education and standard of living dimensions.
2. It reported a sharp decline in multidimensional poverty between 2013–14 and 2022–23.
3. It measures poverty solely on the basis of household income.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
MPI is non-income based.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of a country is ₹2,66,000 crore and real GDP (at base-year prices) is ₹1,90,000 crore. The GDP deflator is:
questions.x:
GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 = (2,66,000 / 1,90,000) × 100 = 140.
Prices have risen 40% over the base year.

questions.q: In the absence of a partnership deed, a partner who advanced a loan of ₹50,000 to the firm and also worked full-time is entitled to:
o: Interest at 6% p.a. on the loan but no salary
questions.x: Section 13 of the Partnership Act: no remuneration; 6% interest on advances beyond capital.

questions.q:
Consider the following about contingent liabilities:
1. They are disclosed in notes to accounts rather than recognised in the balance sheet.
2. A guarantee given for another company's loan is an example.
3. They are always recognised as provisions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A provision is recognised only when an outflow is probable and can be reliably estimated.

questions.q: A computer server is purchased for ₹2,65,000 and ₹12,000 is spent on its installation. Its estimated useful life is 8 years with a residual value of ₹14,000. Annual depreciation under the Straight Line Method is:
questions.x:
SLM depreciation = (Cost + installation − residual value) / useful life.
= (2,65,000 + 12,000 − 14,000) / 8 = 2,63,000 / 8 = ₹32,875 per year.
Installation is capitalised as part of cost (AS 10 / Ind AS 16).

questions.q: A firm earns an average profit of ₹63,000 on capital employed of ₹2,00,000. The normal rate of return in the industry is 15%. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit is:

A company forfeited 100 shares of ₹10 each (₹8 called up) on which ₹5 had been received. 60 of these were reissued as fully paid at ₹9 per share. The amount transferred to capital reserve on reissue is:
questions.x: Forfeiture credited ₹5 × 100 = ₹500. On reissue of 60 shares, the discount allowed is ₹1 per share (₹60). Forfeited amount on these 60 = ₹300; transfer to capital reserve = 300 − 60 = ₹240.

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 5 : 4. They admit R for a 1/8 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
The primary objective of an independent financial audit is to:
o: Express an opinion on whether the financial statements give a true and fair view
questions.x: Fraud detection is incidental; the auditor gives reasonable, not absolute, assurance.

questions.q: Debtors turnover ratio is 8 times. Taking a 360-day year, the average collection period is:

A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹2,65,000 and at the end ₹2,65,000. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹10,000 and withdrew ₹20,000 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 2,65,000 + 20,000 − 10,000 − 2,65,000 = ₹10,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: A trial balance shows Capital ₹2,00,000 (credit) and Drawings ₹30,000 (debit); net profit for the year is ₹50,000. Closing capital is:

Consider the following statements about strikes under the IR Code, 2020:
1. Notice of strike is required only in public utility services.
2. A strike cannot be held during the pendency of conciliation proceedings and for seven days after their conclusion.
3. Mass casual leave by half or more of the workers on a given day is treated as a strike.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is incorrect; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
The IR Code extended the notice requirement to all industrial establishments; statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: The ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (1998) was amended in 2022 to add:
o: A safe and healthy working environment
questions.x: Correct answer: A safe and healthy working environment. This made C155 and C187 fundamental conventions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act:
1. It was not subsumed into any of the four Labour Codes.
2. A child below 14 may help the family in a family enterprise after school hours, in non-hazardous work.
3. Adolescents aged 14–18 may be employed in hazardous occupations with parental consent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Adolescents cannot be employed in the listed hazardous occupations and processes, consent notwithstanding.

questions.q:
Consider the following about deductions under the Code on Wages, 2019:
1. Total deductions in a wage period ordinarily cannot exceed 50% of the wages.
2. A fine may be imposed for any act or omission, with or without prior approval of the specified acts.
3. Recovery of an advance of wages is an authorised deduction.
4. A fine must be recovered within ninety days of the act or omission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct; Statement 4 is correct.
Fines are allowed only for acts and omissions specified in a notice approved by the appropriate government; the 50% cap, recovery of advances and the 90-day recovery limit are correct.

questions.q: In a district, the population is 20 lakh, the labour force 9 lakh and employed persons 8.55 lakh. What are the LFPR, WPR and unemployment rate respectively?
An employee's salary is ₹16,000 per month and the notified minimum wage for the job is ₹9,000. The establishment declares 12% bonus. The annual bonus computed under the statutory ceiling is:
questions.x: Salary for computation is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher → ₹9,000. Bonus = 9,000 × 12 × 12% = ₹12,960.

questions.q: A company with 250 workers decides to close down. Under the IR Code, which of the following is required?
o: Ninety days' notice and permission of the Industrial Tribunal
Sixty days' notice to the government before closure, and closure compensation to workers
questions.x: Prior permission is needed only in establishments with 300 or more workers. For 50–299 workers, 60 days' notice of closure is required, plus compensation.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Factories Act, 1948 (now in the OSH Code):
1. It required a welfare officer in factories with 500 or more workers.
2. It required a canteen in factories with more than 250 workers.
3. It required a creche in factories with 30 or more women workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
These were the Factories Act thresholds; the OSH Code and rules revise several of them.

questions.q: A worker is paid ₹600 per day for an 8-hour day. In a week, the worker works 8 hours on five days and 11 hours on one day. The overtime payment due under the Code on Wages is:
questions.x: Hourly rate = ₹75. Overtime = 3 hours at twice the rate = 3 × 150 = ₹450.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Courts have held that government employees have no fundamental right to strike.
Reason (R): The right to form unions under Article 19(1)(c) does not include the right to achieve every objective of the union, such as striking.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. This reasoning, from All India Bank Employees' Association (1962), underlies later rulings like T.K. Rangarajan (2003).

questions.q: An OSH Code inspector finds that a factory with a hazardous process has no safety committee. Which statement is correct?
o: Only factories with 1,000 or more workers need them
Safety committees are required only in mines
Safety committees with equal management and worker representation are required in factories carrying on hazardous processes
questions.x: Safety committees are required in notified establishments, including factories carrying on hazardous processes.

questions.q:
Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a person employed in a public utility service could not go on strike:
1. Without giving notice of strike within six weeks before striking.
2. Within fourteen days of giving such notice.
3. During the pendency of conciliation proceedings and seven days after their conclusion.
Which of the above restrictions applied?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Section 22 contained all three restrictions; the IR Code now applies the 60-day/14-day notice rule to all industrial establishments.

questions.q: A worker employed through a contractor claims that the factory owner is the real employer because the owner supervises the work, pays through the contractor and owns the tools. Which judgment supports looking at the 'real employer' behind such arrangements?
o: Kameshwar Prasad v. State of Bihar (1962)
Excel Wear v. Union of India (1978)
Hussainbhai v. Alath Factory Thozhilali Union (1978)
questions.x: Hussainbhai held that where the owner controls and benefits from the work, interposition of intermediaries does not defeat the employment relationship.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Labour Codes provide for registration of establishments through a single, electronic process.
Reason (R): Separate registration under multiple Acts raised compliance costs, especially for small establishments.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Simplification of compliance is the rationale.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the EDLI Scheme, 1976:
1. The employee contributes 0.5% of wages.
2. The maximum assurance benefit is ₹7 lakh.
3. An employer may be exempted if a group insurance scheme gives better benefits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is incorrect; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
The employee does not contribute; the employer pays 0.5% of wages.

questions.q:
Consider the following about NPS Vatsalya:
1. It allows parents to open an NPS account for a minor.
2. The account converts to a regular NPS account when the child turns 18.
3. It is administered by EPFO.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
NPS Vatsalya is regulated by PFRDA.

questions.q:
Consider the following about gig and platform workers under the Code on Social Security, 2020:
1. Aggregators contribute 1–2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of the amount payable to such workers.
2. A National Social Security Board advises on schemes for them.
3. They are treated as regular employees of the platform.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Code defines them separately from employees.

questions.q: Under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995, a member retires at 58 with pensionable salary of ₹12,500 and pensionable service of 33 years (including any weightage). The monthly member pension is:
questions.x:
Monthly pension = (Pensionable salary × Pensionable service) / 70
= (12,500 × 33) / 70 = ₹5,893.
Pensionable salary is the average of the last 60 months' wages (subject to the ₹15,000 ceiling), and the minimum pension is ₹1,000.

questions.q: Arrange the following in chronological order: 1. ESI Act 2. EPF Act 3. Payment of Gratuity Act 4. Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act
questions.x: Correct answer: 1, 2, 3, 4. ESI (1948), EPF (1952), Gratuity (1972), UWSS (2008).

questions.q: An insured woman under ESI and a woman under the Maternity Benefit Act both deliver their first child. Which statement is correct?
o: Only the ESI-covered woman gets 26 weeks
The MB Act applies to ESI-covered women in addition, so she gets 52 weeks
Both are entitled to 26 weeks; under ESI the benefit is paid by ESIC, under the MB Act by the employer
questions.x: An employee covered by ESI gets maternity benefit from ESIC; the MB Act does not apply to such employees for the same benefit.

questions.q: An employee draws basic wages plus DA of ₹40,000 per month and both employer and employee contribute 12% on actual wages. How much of the employer's share goes to the EPF (provident fund) account each month?
questions.x:
Employer's 12% of 40,000 = ₹4,800.
EPS share is capped at 8.33% of ₹15,000 = ₹1,250.
EPF share = 4,800 − 1,250 = ₹3,550.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹13,500 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹6,500 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 12%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 6,500) = ₹7,000.
Salary for computation = min(13,500, 7,000) = ₹7,000.
Annual bonus = 7,000 × 12 × 12% = ₹10,080. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q:
Consider the following about a Universal Basic Income (UBI):
1. The Economic Survey 2016-17 discussed UBI as an idea for India.
2. A UBI is paid unconditionally to individuals.
3. India has implemented a nationwide UBI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India has not adopted UBI.

questions.q:
Which of the following schemes are presently framed and in operation under the EPF & MP Act, 1952?
1. Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952
2. Employees' Family Pension Scheme, 1971
3. Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976
4. Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995
How many of the above are in operation?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The Family Pension Scheme, 1971 was replaced by EPS 1995; the other three are in operation.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Edge computing is useful for self-driving vehicles.
Reason (R): Decisions must be taken within milliseconds, without waiting for a distant data centre.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Local processing cuts latency.

questions.q:
Consider the following about vaccines:
1. mRNA vaccines instruct cells to make a viral protein that triggers an immune response.
2. mRNA vaccines change the DNA of the person vaccinated.
3. The measles vaccine is a live attenuated vaccine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
mRNA does not enter the nucleus or alter DNA.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Hilly areas take longer to cook rice in an open pot.
Reason (R): Atmospheric pressure is lower at high altitude, so water boils below 100 °C.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. A lower boiling temperature means slower cooking.

questions.q:
Consider the following about hardness of water:
1. Temporary hardness is due to bicarbonates of calcium and magnesium and can be removed by boiling.
2. Permanent hardness is due to chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium.
3. Hard water forms lather easily with soap.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Hard water forms scum with soap and lathers poorly.

questions.q:
Consider the following about IP addressing:
1. An IPv4 address is 32 bits long.
2. An IPv6 address is 128 bits long.
3. IPv6 was introduced because the IPv4 address space was running out.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
IPv6 allows about 3.4 × 10³⁸ addresses.

questions.q: If cell A1 contains 75, what does =IF(A1>=60, "Pass", "Fail") return?
questions.x: Correct answer: Pass. The condition is true, so the second argument is returned.

questions.q:
Consider the following about seismic waves:
1. P-waves can travel through solids, liquids and gases.
2. S-waves cannot travel through liquids.
3. The S-wave shadow zone indicates that the outer core is liquid.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
This reasoning is the main evidence for a liquid outer core.

questions.q: An earthquake of magnitude 7 releases roughly how much more energy than one of magnitude 5?
questions.x: Each unit of magnitude means about 32 times more energy; 32 × 32 ≈ 1,000.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): HIV weakens the immune system over time.
Reason (R): HIV infects and destroys CD4 helper T cells, which coordinate immune responses.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Falling CD4 counts lead to AIDS.

questions.q: A household replaces ten 60 W bulbs with ten 9 W LED lamps, each used 5 hours a day. About how many units (kWh) are saved in 30 days?

Consider the following about ethanol blending in India:
1. India achieved about 20% ethanol blending in petrol in 2025.
2. Ethanol is produced from sugarcane juice, molasses and grains.
3. Ethanol has a higher energy content per litre than petrol.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Ethanol has lower energy per litre, which slightly reduces mileage.

questions.q: A circuit outputs 0 only when both inputs are 1, and 1 otherwise. Which gate is it?
questions.x: That is the NAND truth table.

questions.q: The average of 11 observations is 46. The average of the first 6 is 40 and that of the last 6 is 57. The 6th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 11 = 11 × 46 = 506.
First 6 + last 6 = 6×40 + 6×57 = 582; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 582 − 506 = 76.

questions.q: Find the remainder when 3^195 is divided by 9.
A, B and C can complete a contract alone in 6, 24 and 14 days respectively. Working together they finish it and receive ₹32,900. If payment is in proportion to the work done, C's share is:
questions.x:
Daily work rates are 1/6 : 1/24 : 1/14 = 28 : 7 : 12 (LCM 168).
Working together, work done is in the same ratio, so C gets 12/47 × 32,900 = ₹8,400.

questions.q: A bag has 4 white and 13 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(13,2)/C(17,2) = 78/136.
Required = 1 − 39/68 = 29/68.

questions.q: Two trains of lengths 240 m and 230 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 36 km/h and 54 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.x:
Opposite directions → relative speed = 36 + 54 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s.
Distance = sum of lengths = 470 m.
Time = 470 / 25 = 18.8 s.

questions.q: What is the least number which, when divided by 6, 15, 18, leaves a remainder of 3 in each case?
questions.x: Required number = LCM(6, 15, 18) + 3 = 90 + 3 = 93.

questions.q: Two trains start at the same time from stations X and Y towards each other. After they cross, they take 16 hours and 81 hours respectively to reach Y and X. The ratio of the speed of the train from X to that of the train from Y is:
questions.x:
Standard result: S₁ : S₂ = √t₂ : √t₁, where t₁ and t₂ are the times taken after meeting.
= √81 : √16 = 9 : 4 = 9 : 4.

questions.q: In a certain code, 'A $ B' means A is the brother of B; 'A ÷ B' means A is the daughter of B; 'A + B' means A is the sister of B; 'A # B' means A is the son of B. If 'Q ÷ P $ N' (read as Q ÷ P and P $ N), how is Q related to N?
questions.x:
Q ÷ P: Q is the daughter of P. P $ N: P is the brother of N.
Combining the two (all persons taken to be of one family, as is conventional): Q is the niece of N.

questions.q: On which day of the week did 13 September 1997 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 1996: 1600 years → 0 odd days; 300 years → 1; remaining 96 years have 24 leap + 72 ordinary → 24×2 + 72 = 120 → 1 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 1997 up to 13 September = 256 → 4 odd day(s).
Total = 1 + 1 + 4 = 6 → 6 → Saturday.

questions.q: Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010 and log₁₀ 3 = 0.4771, how many digits are there in 24^47?
questions.x:
log₁₀(24^47) = 47 × log₁₀ 24 = 47 × 1.3802 = 64.8694.
The characteristic is 64, so the number of digits = 64 + 1 = 65.

questions.q: The monthly salary of a clerk rises by 10%, then falls by 10%, and finally rises by 5%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 10/100) × (1 − 10/100) × (1 + 5/100) = 1.1 × 0.9 × 1.05 = 1.0395.
Overall change = (1.0395 − 1) × 100 = 3.95% → 3.95% increase.
Note: simply adding (10 − 10 + 5) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: Asha and Bhavna together can paint a hall in 8 days. Asha alone can do it in 10 days. How many days will Bhavna alone take?
questions.x:
Bhavna's one-day work = 1/8 − 1/10 = (10 − 8)/80 = 1/40.
So Bhavna alone takes 40 days.

questions.q: Find the next term in the series: E3H, H6K, K12N, N21Q, ?
questions.x:
First letters advance by 3 (E, H, K, N, Q); the last letter is always 3 places after the first; the numbers increase by 3, 6, 9, … (3, 6, 12, 21, 33).
Next term: Q33T.

questions.q: At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 10 years. In how many years will it become 3 times itself at the same rate?
questions.x:
Doubling means interest = 1 × principal in 10 years, i.e. rate = 100/10 = 10% p.a.
To become 3 times, interest must be 2 × principal.
Time = (2 × 100) / 10 = 20 years. (Rule: time ∝ number of times the principal is earned as interest.)

questions.q: In a row, Imran is 10th from the left and Rekha is 9th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Imran becomes 21st from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Imran occupies Rekha's old place, which is 9th from the right and now 21st from the left.
Total = 21 + 9 − 1 = 29.

questions.q: A invests ₹30,000 for the whole year and B invests ₹30,000 after 5 months. If the annual profit is ₹15,200, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 30,000×12, B: 30,000×7 → 12 : 7.
B's share = 7/19 × 15,200 = ₹5,600.
